L506: Besides having an x and y location, a window also has a location in the z dimension, which determines its vertical position with respect to other windows. This is known as the window's z-order, and there are two types: normal z-order and topmost z-order. The location of a window in the normal z-order is determined by whether it's currently active or not. By default, a window is located in the normal z-order.
L507: The location of a window in the topmost z-order is also determined by whether it's currently active or not. Furthermore, windows in the topmost z-order are always located above windows in the normal z-order. A window is located in the topmost z-order by setting its 【21†Topmost】 property to `true`.
L508: Within each z-order type, the currently active window appears above all other windows in the same z-order.
L509: ## Window size
L510: 
L511: Besides having a desktop location, a window has a size that is determined by several properties, including the various width and height properties and 【51†SizeToContent】.
L512: 
L513: 【52†MinWidth】, 【53†Width】, and 【54†MaxWidth】 are used to manage the range of widths that a window can have during its lifetime.
L514: 
L515:     `<Window
L516:         xmlns="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml/presentation"
L517:         MinWidth="300" Width="400" MaxWidth="500">
L518:     </Window>
L519:     `
L520: Window height is managed by 【55†MinHeight】, 【56†Height】, and 【57†MaxHeight】.
L521: 
L522:     `<Window
L523:         xmlns="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml/presentation"
L524:         MinHeight="300" Height="400" MaxHeight="500">
L525:     </Window>
L526:     `
L527: Because the various width values and height values each specify a range, it's possible for the width and height of a resizable window to be anywhere within the specified range for the respective dimension. To detect its current width and height, inspect 【58†ActualWidth】 and 【59†ActualHeight】, respectively.
L528: 
L529: If you'd like the width and height of your window to have a size that fits to the size of the window's content, you can use the 【51†SizeToContent】 property, which has the following values:
L530:   * 【60†SizeToContent.Manual】
L531: No effect (default).
L532:   * 【61†SizeToContent.Width】
L533: Fit to content width, which has the same effect as setting both 【52†MinWidth】 and 【54†MaxWidth】 to the width of the content.
L534:   * 【62†SizeToContent.Height】
L535: Fit to content height, which has the same effect as setting both 【55†MinHeight】 and 【57†MaxHeight】 to the height of the content.
L536:   * 【63†SizeToContent.WidthAndHeight】
L537: Fit to content width and height, which has the same effect as setting both 【55†MinHeight】 and 【57†MaxHeight】 to the height of the content, and setting both 【52†MinWidth】 and 【54†MaxWidth】 to the width of the content.
L538: The following example shows a window that automatically sizes to fit its content, both vertically and horizontally, when first shown.
L539: 
L540:     `<Window
L541:         xmlns="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml/presentation"
L542:         SizeToContent="WidthAndHeight">
L543:     </Window>
L544:     `
L545: The following example shows how to set the 【51†SizeToContent】 property in code to specify how a window resizes to fit its content .
L546: 
L547:     `// Manually alter window height and width
L548:     this.SizeToContent = SizeToContent.Manual;
L549: 
L550:     // Automatically resize width relative to content
L551:     this.SizeToContent = SizeToContent.Width;
L552: 
L553:     // Automatically resize height relative to content
L554:     this.SizeToContent = SizeToContent.Height;
L555:     // Automatically resize height and width relative to content
L556:     this.SizeToContent = SizeToContent.WidthAndHeight;
L557:     `
L558: 
L559:     `' Manually alter window height and width
L560:     Me.SizeToContent = SizeToContent.Manual
L561: 
L562:     ' Automatically resize width relative to content
L563:     Me.SizeToContent = SizeToContent.Width
L564: 
L565:     ' Automatically resize height relative to content
L566:     Me.SizeToContent = SizeToContent.Height
L567: 
L568:     ' Automatically resize height and width relative to content
L569:     Me.SizeToContent = SizeToContent.WidthAndHeight
L570:     `
L571: ## Order of precedence for sizing properties
L572: 
L573: Essentially, the various sizes properties of a window combine to define the range of width and height for a resizable window. To ensure a valid range is maintained, 【5†Window】 evaluates the values of the size properties using the following orders of precedence.
L574: 
L575: For Height Properties:
L576: 
L577:   1. 【55†FrameworkElement.MinHeight】
L578:   2. 【57†FrameworkElement.MaxHeight】
L579:   3. 【62†SizeToContent.Height】 / 【63†SizeToContent.WidthAndHeight】
L580:   4. 【56†FrameworkElement.Height】
L581: For Width Properties:
L582: 
L583:   1. 【52†FrameworkElement.MinWidth】
L584:   2. 【54†FrameworkElement.MaxWidth】
L585:   3. 【61†SizeToContent.Width】 / 【63†SizeToContent.WidthAndHeight】
L586:   4. 【53†FrameworkElement.Width】
L587: 
L588: The order of precedence can also determine the size of a window when it's maximized, which is managed with the 【64†WindowState】 property.
L589: ## Window state
L590: 
L591: During the lifetime of a resizable window, it can have three states: normal, minimized, and maximized. A window with a normal state is the default state of a window. A window with this state allows a user to move and resize it by using a resize grip or the border, if it's resizable.
L592: A window with a minimized state collapses to its task bar button if 【65†ShowInTaskbar】 is set to `true`; otherwise, it collapses to the smallest possible size it can be and moves itself to the bottom-left corner of the desktop. Neither type of minimized window can be resized using a border or resize grip, although a minimized window that isn't shown in the task bar can be dragged around the desktop.
L593: A window with a maximized state expands to the maximum size it can be, which will only be as large as its 【54†MaxWidth】, 【57†MaxHeight】, and 【51†SizeToContent】 properties dictate. Like a minimized window, a maximized window can't be resized by using a resize grip or by dragging the border.
L594: 
L595: Note
L596: 
L597: The values of the 【45†Top】, 【44†Left】, 【53†Width】, and 【56†Height】 properties of a window always represent the values for the normal state, even when the window is currently maximized or minimized.
L598: The state of a window can be configured by setting its 【64†WindowState】 property, which can have one of the following 【66†WindowState】 enumeration values:
L599: 
L600:   * 【67†Normal】 (default)
L601:   * 【68†Maximized】
L602:   * 【69†Minimized】
L603: 
L604: The following example shows how to create a window that is shown as maximized when it opens.
L605: 
L606:     `<Window
L607:         xmlns="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml/presentation"
L608:         WindowState="Maximized">
L609:     </Window>
L610:     `
L611: In general, you should set 【64†WindowState】 to configure the initial state of a window. Once a resizable window is shown, users can press the minimize, maximize, and restore buttons on the window's title bar to change the window state.
L612: ## Window appearance
L613: 
L614: You change the appearance of the client area of a window by adding window-specific content to it, such as buttons, labels, and text boxes. To configure the non-client area, 【5†Window】 provides several properties, which include 【70†Icon】 to set a window's icon and 【71†Title】 to set its title.
L615: 
L616: You can also change the appearance and behavior of non-client area border by configuring a window's resize mode, window style, and whether it appears as a button in the desktop task bar.
L617: ### Resize mode
L618: 
L619: Depending on the 【72†WindowStyle】 property, you can control if, and how, users resize the window. The window style affects the following:
L620: 
L621:   * Allow or disallow resizing by dragging the window border with the mouse.
L622:   * Whether the Minimize, Maximize, and Close buttons appear on the non-client area.
L623:   * Whether the Minimize, Maximize, and Close buttons are enabled.
L624: You can configure how a window resizes by setting its 【73†ResizeMode】 property, which can be one of the following 【74†ResizeMode】 enumeration values:
L625: 
L626:   * 【75†NoResize】
L627:   * 【76†CanMinimize】
L628:   * 【77†CanResize】 (default)
L629:   * 【78†CanResizeWithGrip】
L630: As with 【72†WindowStyle】, the resize mode of a window is unlikely to change during its lifetime, which means that you'll most likely set it from XAML markup.
L631: 
L632:     `<Window
L633:         xmlns="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml/presentation"
L634:         ResizeMode="CanResizeWithGrip">
L635:     </Window>
L636:     `
L637: 
L638: Note that you can detect whether a window is maximized, minimized, or restored by inspecting the 【64†WindowState】 property.

L272: ## Remarks
L273: 
L274: Use 【17†FileSystemWatcher】 to watch for changes in a specified directory. You can watch for changes in files and subdirectories of the specified directory. You can create a component to watch files on a local computer, a network drive, or a remote computer.
L275: To watch for changes in all files, set the 【18†Filter】 property to an empty string (`""`) or use wildcards (`"*.*"`). To watch a specific file, set the 【18†Filter】 property to the file name. For example, to watch for changes in the file MyDoc.txt, set the 【18†Filter】 property to `"MyDoc.txt"`. You can also watch for changes in a certain type of file. For example, to watch for changes in text files, set the 【18†Filter】 property to `"*.txt"`.
L276: There are several types of changes you can watch for in a directory or file. For example, you can watch for changes in `Attributes`, the `LastWrite` date and time, or the `Size` of files or directories. This is done by setting the 【19†NotifyFilter】 property to one of the 【20†NotifyFilters】 values. For more information on the type of changes you can watch, see 【20†NotifyFilters】.
L277: You can watch for renaming, deletion, or creation of files or directories. For example, to watch for renaming of text files, set the 【18†Filter】 property to "*.txt" and call the 【21†WaitForChanged】 method with a 【22†Renamed】 specified for its parameter.
L278: The Windows operating system notifies your component of file changes in a buffer created by the 【17†FileSystemWatcher】. If there are many changes in a short time, the buffer can overflow. This causes the component to lose track of changes in the directory, and it will only provide blanket notification.
L279: Increasing the size of the buffer with the 【23†InternalBufferSize】 property is expensive, as it comes from non-paged memory that cannot be swapped out to disk, so keep the buffer as small yet large enough to not miss any file change events. To avoid a buffer overflow, use the 【19†NotifyFilter】 and 【24†IncludeSubdirectories】 properties so you can filter out unwanted change notifications.
L280: For a list of initial property values for an instance of 【17†FileSystemWatcher】, see the 【25†FileSystemWatcher】 constructor.
L281: 
L282: Consider the following facts when you use the 【17†FileSystemWatcher】 class:
L283:   * Hidden files aren't ignored.
L284:   * In some systems, 【17†FileSystemWatcher】 reports changes to files using the short 8.3 file name format. For example, a change to "LongFileName.LongExtension" could be reported as "LongFil~.Lon".
L285:   * The maximum size you can set for the 【23†InternalBufferSize】 property for monitoring a directory over the network is 64 KB.
L286: ### Copy and move folders
L287: 
L288: The operating system and 【17†FileSystemWatcher】 object interpret a cut-and-paste action or a move action as a rename action for a folder and its contents. If you cut and paste a folder with files into a folder being watched, the 【17†FileSystemWatcher】 object reports only the folder as new, but not its contents because they are essentially only renamed.
L289: To be notified that the contents of folders have been moved or copied into a watched folder, provide 【26†OnChanged】 and 【27†OnRenamed】 event handler methods as suggested in the following table.
L290: 
L291: Event Handler  | Events Handled  | Performs
L292: --- | --- | ---
L293: 【26†OnChanged】  | 【28†Changed】, 【29†Created】, 【30†Deleted】  | Report changes in file attributes, created files, and deleted files.
L294: 【27†OnRenamed】  | 【31†Renamed】  | List the old and new paths of renamed files and folders, expanding recursively if needed.
L295: ### Events and buffer sizes
L296: 
L297: Note that several factors can affect which file system change events are raised, as described by the following:
L298:   * Common file system operations might raise more than one event. For example, when a file is moved from one directory to another, several 【26†OnChanged】 and some 【32†OnCreated】 and 【33†OnDeleted】 events might be raised. Moving a file is a complex operation that consists of multiple simple operations, therefore raising multiple events. Likewise, some applications (for example, antivirus software) might cause additional file system events that are detected by 【17†FileSystemWatcher】.
L299:   * The 【17†FileSystemWatcher】 can watch disks as long as they are not switched or removed. The 【17†FileSystemWatcher】 does not raise events for CDs and DVDs, because time stamps and properties cannot change. Remote computers must have one of the required platforms installed for the component to function properly.
L300: Note that a 【17†FileSystemWatcher】 may miss an event when the buffer size is exceeded. To avoid missing events, follow these guidelines:
L301: 
L302:   * Increase the buffer size by setting the 【23†InternalBufferSize】 property.
L303:   * Avoid watching files with long file names, because a long file name contributes to filling up the buffer. Consider renaming these files using shorter names.
L304:   * Keep your event handling code as short as possible.
L305: ## Constructors
L306: 
L307: Name  | Description
L308: --- | ---
L309: 【34†FileSystemWatcher()】  | Initializes a new instance of the 【17†FileSystemWatcher】 class.
L310: 【35†FileSystemWatcher(String, String)】  | Initializes a new instance of the 【17†FileSystemWatcher】 class, given the specified directory and type of files to monitor.
L311: 【36†FileSystemWatcher(String)】  | Initializes a new instance of the 【17†FileSystemWatcher】 class, given the specified directory to monitor.
L312: ## Properties

L315: 【37†CanRaiseEvents】  | Gets a value indicating whether the component can raise an event. (Inherited from 【13†Component】)

L319: 【42†Events】  | Gets the list of event handlers that are attached to this 【13†Component】. (Inherited from 【13†Component】)
L320: 【18†Filter】  | Gets or sets the filter string used to determine what files are monitored in a directory.
L321: 【43†Filters】  | Gets the collection of all the filters used to determine what files are monitored in a directory.
L322: 【24†IncludeSubdirectories】  | Gets or sets a value indicating whether subdirectories within the specified path should be monitored.
L323: 【23†InternalBufferSize】  | Gets or sets the size (in bytes) of the internal buffer.
L324: 【19†NotifyFilter】  | Gets or sets the type of changes to watch for.
L325: 【44†Path】  | Gets or sets the path of the directory to watch.
L326: 【45†Site】  | Gets or sets an 【46†ISite】 for the 【17†FileSystemWatcher】.
L327: 【47†SynchronizingObject】  | Gets or sets the object used to marshal the event handler calls issued as a result of a directory change.

L0: # Getting Started Guide
L1: 
L2: This guide will walk you through installing Kopia and setting up Kopia to backup/restore your data. Make sure to familiarize yourself with Kopia 【0†features】 before following this guide, so that you understand the appropriate terminology. As a reminder:
L3:   * A `snapshot` is a 【1†point-in-time backup】 of your files/directories; each snapshot contains the files/directories that you can 【2†restore when you need to】.
L4:   * A `repository` is the storage location where your snapshots are saved; Kopia supports 【3†cloud/remote, network, and local storage locations】 and all repositories are 【4†encrypted】 with a password that you designate.
L5:   * A `policy` is a set of rules that tells Kopia how to create/manage snapshots; this includes features such as 【5†compression, snapshot retention, and scheduling when to take automatically snapshots】.
L6: ## Download and Installation
L7: 
L8: Read the 【6†download and installation guide】 to learn how to download & install Kopia. As a reminder, Kopia comes in two variants: 【7†command-line interface (CLI)】 and 【7†graphical user interface (GUI)】. Pick the one you like the most.
L9: 
L10: ## Setting Up Kopia
L11: 
L12: Once you have installed Kopia, setting up Kopia is quite easy but varies depending on if you are using Kopia CLI or Kopia GUI (also known as `KopiaUI`).
L13: ### Kopia GUI (`KopiaUI`)
L14: 
L15: Setting up Kopia via the GUI is very easy.
L16: #### Creating and Connecting to a Repository
L17: When you run `KopiaUI` for the first time, you will need to create a `repository`. You will see all supported 【8†repository types】 on-screen within the program interface. Pick the one you want and follow the on-screen directions to get it setup. You will need to enter details about the storage location that you selected, and you will pick a password that will be used to encrypt all the snapshots that you store in the repository.
L18: Kopia uses 【9†end-to-end encryption】, that way your password never leaves your machine nor is sent elsewhere. You can name your repository in a way that is useful for you.
L19: Remember your repository password and keep it secure. There is absolutely no way to restore any of your backed up files from a repository if you forget your password!
L20: > NOTE: Remember, before you use Kopia, you need to provision, setup, and pay (the storage provider) for whatever storage location you want to use; Kopia will not do that for you. After you have done that, you can create a `repository` for that storage location in Kopia. For example, if you want to use a cloud storage provider, then you need to: (1) create an account with your storage provider; (2) create an object storage bucket; and (3) get the credentials to access the bucket.
L21: After you have set up your storage provider, then you can select the appropriate storage provider type in `KopiaUI` to create a repository.
L22: #### Defining Snapshot Policy and Creating New Snapshot
L23: Once you have created a repository, you can start backing up your files/directories by creating a new `policy` in `KopiaUI`.
L24: You can do this from the `Policies` tab and the process, again, is quite straightforward: enter the `directory` which contains the files you want to backup (you can either manually type in the `directory path` or browse for the `directory`), hit the `Set Policy` button, choose your policy settings from the on-screen options (all policy options are fairly self-explanatory), and hit the `Save Policy` button.
L25: Kopia will then automatically begin taking the snapshot following the settings you set for the policy.
L26: After the initial snapshot, for every snapshot afterwards Kopia will rescan the file/directories and 【10†only upload file content that has changed】. All snapshots in Kopia are 【10†always incremental】; a snapshot will only upload files/file contents that are not in the repository yet, which saves storage space and upload time. This even applies to files that were moved or renamed.
L27: In fact, if two computers have exactly the same file and both computers are backing up to the same `repository`, the file will still be stored only once.
L28: > PRO TIP: If you pick a value for `Snapshot Frequency` when creating a `policy`, then Kopia will automatically take snapshots at that frequency (e.g., every one hour or whatever value you pick), and you do not need to remember to manually run the snapshot. If you do not pick a `Snapshot Frequency`, then Kopia will not automatically take snapshots, and you need to manually run snapshots from the `Snapshots` tab (just click the `Snapshot Now` button as needed).
L29: Note that you can set policies at four levels in `KopiaUI`:
L30: 
L31:   * at the `global` level (shown with `*` for `Username`, `Host` and `Path`),
L32:   * at the per-host `@host` level (shown with `*` for `Username` and `Path`),
L33:   * at the per-user `user@host` level (shown with `*` for `Path`),
L34:   * and at the individual `Path` level, where the settings are applied only to that particular policy.
L35: By default, all new policies are set to inherit settings from the `global` policy, as well as from the applicable per-host and per-user policies. More specific policies settings take priority. This means that individual per-path policies settings come first, followed by per-user, then per-host and finally global policy settings.
L36: For example, say you have a path policy for `foo@bar:/path` which doesn’t define setting `xyz`, a per-user policy for `foo@bar` setting `xyz` to `1` and the global policy setting `xyz` to `2`. In this case, the effective value of `xyz` for the policy `foo@bar:/path` will be `1`.

L24: You can see that restic processed 1.720 GiB of data; this is the size of the files and directories in `~/work` on the local file system. It also reports that only 1.200 GiB was added to the repository. This means that some of the data was duplicate and restic was able to efficiently reduce it. The data compression also managed to compress the data down to 1.103 GiB.
L25: If you don’t pass the `--verbose` option, restic will print less data. You’ll still get a nice live status display that looks like this:
L26: 
L27:     [0:34] 2.96%  867 files 5.046 GiB, total 307867 files 170.438 GiB, 0 errors ETA 18:35
L28: The progress bar shows, from left to right: elapsed time, progress in percent, the number of files already processed and their size on the local filesystem, followed by the total expected file count and size for the whole backup (these totals come from the initial scan used for progress estimation, which can be disabled with `--no-scan`). Next is a counter for the number of files that caused errors (these are logged above the progress bar), and finally an estimated time of completion.
L29: The file paths displayed below the progress bar are the files currently being read by restic.
L30: Be aware that the live status shows the processed files and not the transferred data. Transferred volume might be lower (due to deduplication) or higher.
L31: On Windows, the `--use-fs-snapshot` option will use Windows’ Volume Shadow Copy Service (VSS) when creating backups. Restic will transparently create a VSS snapshot for each volume that contains files to backup. Files are read from the VSS snapshot instead of the regular filesystem. This allows to backup files that are exclusively locked by another process during the backup.
L32: 
L33: You can use the following extended options to change the VSS behavior:
L34: >   * `-o vss.timeout` specifies timeout for VSS snapshot creation, default value being 120 seconds
L35: >
L36: >   * `-o vss.exclude-all-mount-points` disable auto snapshotting of all volume mount points
L37: >
L38: >   * `-o vss.exclude-volumes` allows excluding specific volumes or volume mount points from snapshotting
L39: >
L40: >   * `-o vss.provider` specifies VSS provider used for snapshotting
L41: For example a 2.5 minutes timeout with snapshotting of mount points disabled can be specified as:
L42: 
L43:     -o vss.timeout=2m30s -o vss.exclude-all-mount-points=true
L44: 
L45: 
L46: and excluding drive `d:\`, mount point `c:\mnt` and volume `\\?\Volume{04ce0545-3391-11e0-ba2f-806e6f6e6963}\` as:
L47: 
L48:     -o vss.exclude-volumes="d:;c:\mnt\;\\?\volume{04ce0545-3391-11e0-ba2f-806e6f6e6963}"
L49: 
L50: 
L51: VSS provider can be specified by GUID:
L52: 
L53:     -o vss.provider={3f900f90-00e9-440e-873a-96ca5eb079e5}
L54: or by name:
L55: 
L56:     -o vss.provider="Hyper-V IC Software Shadow Copy Provider"
L57: 
L58: 
L59: Also, `MS` can be used as alias for `Microsoft Software Shadow Copy provider 1.0`.
L60: 
L61: By default VSS ignores Outlook OST files. This is not a restriction of restic but the default Windows VSS configuration. The files not to snapshot are configured in the Windows registry under the following key:
L62: 
L63:     HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\BackupRestore\FilesNotToSnapshot
L64: For more details refer to the official Windows documentation e.g. the article `Registry Keys and Values for Backup and Restore`.
